title: 3D File (OBJ) Import/Export
content: ### OBJ Import/Export ### Objective An OBJ file is used when saving Scene and Props that organize Avatar and surrounding environment. If the OBJ type is an Avatar, the OBJ file is able to wear Garments but if it is a Trim, the Garment passes through it as it does not recognize it as an object. For detailed instruction on how to use OBJ files as Trims, refer to Load As Trim. Furthermore, OBJ files with the same Mesh structure (net-shaped structure expresses 3D objects) is able to be "Morphed" to change Avatar's appearance. “Morphing” refers to slowly changing the appearance of one object into another, and this function can be used to change Avatar's poses or body type. This function is useful when changing Poses of an Avatar in Garments. For detailed instruction, refer to Load as Morph Target. Garments made with Marvelous Designer are able to be formatted/imported in *.obj file and they are compatible with other 3D software. When exporting Garments in an *.obj file, a *.mtl file is also created, and this *.mtl file saves material information of the Garment. ### Location #### OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Additional OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ #### OBJ Export Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ #### Selected OBJ Export Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ (Selected) ### Operation #### OBJ Import 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Select a file and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### OBJ Import Detail Settings Object Type | Load as Avatar | Imports an object as an avatar and replaces it with the original avatar. Add Arrangement Points &BVs: Turn on this option to generate Bounding Volumes and Arrangement Points fit to the imported OBJ (ver4.2.0). ※Note: This option works properly only when imported OBJ is either in T or A pose and below error message appears when this function cannot be applied properly. "Arrangement Points were not fitted to the avatar. The avatar must be in a T-pose or A-pose." ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438250166297) ---|---|--- Load as Trim | Due to nonfunctional collision detection, objects pass through garments (ver3.0.0). Load as Garment | Import an object as a 3D Garment. Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map: Toggle on this option to generate Patterns based on UV Map information (ver4.2.0). Load as Morph Target | Morphs the original object into the object designated as the Morph Target. Enter the Transition Frame Count. The higher the frame count, the slower the morphing process. Scale | Manually enters values or selects the desired unit. Axis Conversion | Changes the directions of each axis of an object. When the OBJ is placed below the ground, please toggle on Align Bottom to Ground option to pull up the OBJ file above the ground (ver4.2.0). ※ Note: Load as Garment - Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map #### OBJ Additional Import 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ → The Add File window appears. 2. Set details and click OK. #### OBJ Export 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ OBJ (Selected) → Save File window appears. 2. Select desired location to store, and click Save. → Export OBJ window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: #### OBJ Export Detail Settings Object | Select All Patterns: Select/Deselect all Patterns. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ※ Note: If OBJ(Selected) is utilized, selected Patterns are being checked in the 3D and 2D window. Select All Avatars: Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). Select All Graphics/Top-stitches: Select/Deselect all Graphics/Top-stitches. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right (ver2.2.0). ---|--- #### Single Object Exports selected object as a single object. | #### Multiple Objects Exports selected object as multiple objects. #### Unweld Exports Vertex(points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects. | #### Weld Combines Vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts together as one point. Weld Selected Pattern: Weld sewing-lines of selected patterns. #### Thin Ensures thickness is not exported to Geometry even if the value is increased beforehand. | #### Thick Exports thickness value to Geometry. ※ Note: Thickness is available to be exported when pattern's mesh is Quad (ver2.3.0). Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. ※Note: Unified Texture (ver3.1.0). Export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information. | Image File | Designate file saving path and file name. Add numbers behind the file name as below: ‘File Name_0’, ‘File Name_1’. ---|--- Texture Size | Width and Height will be saved in a fixed ratio. Allowance: 100 ~ 10000 Pixel Fill Texture Seams | Expands the scope of the texture having its boundary line as the standard. Allowance: 0 ~ 15 mm When you type in values, preview will show in the 2D Window. ※ Weld Turned Sewing Lines (ver 2026.0) Even when the Sewing Line Type is set to Turned, you can still merge vertices for export. Include Internal Shape: Includes internal line and/or shape information in export (ver2.3.0). Scale | Adjusts scale of file being exported when a value is entered or desired unit from 'Unit in file to import' is selected. Axis Conversion | Changes directions of object's each axis. File | Save with Texture File (*.zip): Exports .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation. Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting (ver4.2.0). Exclude Ambient Map & Color (Modo): Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting (ver4.2.0). Save with Alpha Map: Alpha Map is included when exporting (ver4.2.0). Save with Meta Data (*.xml) : Exports garment's pattern(Mesh), physical property and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0). Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: Combine and save garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0). Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo): Exclude Ambient color value when saving materials. ※ Note: #### OBJ Export Updates Internal Line(s)/Shape(s) export (including FBX). Thickness export for Quad Mesh. Front, side and back meshes separate export. * * * ### ### Load as Garment ### Objective Import and simulate OBJ files from other 3D software programs (Maya, 3DS MAX and etc). ### Location Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ to Garment ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add) ▶ OBJ to Garment → Open File window appears. 2. Select a file and click OK. → OBJ to Garment window appears. 3. Set details and click OK. ### Load as Morph Target ### Objective Morph uses two different OBJ files to slowly change object's appearance. Marvelous Designer's default avatars can be modified at Change Avatar Size menu or posed with Show X-Ray Joints function, other 3D software may not have basic Joints set for designed objects, parts may be lost when creating a compatible COLLADA file. As such, this menu can be used to change the object's body type. At least two *.obj files with the same Mesh structure are needed to morph the object. Use this menu to import objects from different 3D software as Avatars, and dress them or change their Poses. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438235048217) ### Location #### Import OBJ Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Open Morph Target OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Morph Target ### Operation 1. Choose two *.obj files to morph. 2. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 3. Select the first file to import and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 4. Set details and click OK. 5. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 6. Select the second file to import and click OK. → Open Morph Target window appears. 7. Follow the indicated guideline: OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Morph Target 8. Set details and click OK. ※ Note: File name with #(special character) is not going to be loaded. ### Load as Trim ### Objective Use *.obj files designed in other 3D software to organize Trims as well as the Avatars in Garments. When loading a file as an Avatar, the Garment registers the object as an Avatar and allows to drape on top of it, however when the same file is loaded as Trims, the Garment does not register it as an object therefore it passes through it. ![Captura](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438250539289) ### Location #### OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Import as Scene/Prop OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Trim ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Choose file to import and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 3. Select Load as Trim in Object Type. 4. Set details and click OK. ### Load as Avatar ### Objective Use *.obj files designed in other 3D software to use as Avatars in Marvelous Designer. When loading a file as an Avatar, the Garment registers the object as an Avatar and allows to drape on top of it. ### Location #### OBJ Import Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ #### Import as Scene/Prop OBJ Import Options Window ▶ Object Type ▶ Load as Avatar ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ OBJ → Open File window appears. 2. Choose file to import and click OK. → Import OBJ window appears. 3. Select Load as Avatar in Object Type. 4. Set details and click OK.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for importing and exporting OBJ files in Marvelous Designer, detailing the functionalities and settings for using these files with Avatars and Garments.

title: Remeshing
content: ### ### Objective Generates aligned automatic Retopology results. (MD 8) ### Location Right click on a pattern (3D window) → Remeshing Right click on a pattern (3D window) → Mesh Style → Quad (Grid) (ver. 2024.0) Pattern property window → Remeshing Pattern property window → Mesh → Mesh Style → Quad (Grid) (ver. 2024.0) ### Operation 1. Find and click the menu indicated in Location. The mesh of the selected pattern is rearranged in an aligned quad mesh. 2. When changing pattern's particle distance, it will be reflected to re-meshed pattern. 3. When rotating a pattern in a 2D window, the meshes are rearranged relative to the X, Y axis of the 2D window. \- After rotating pattern in 2D window, need to Undo Remeshing and apply Remeshing again to reflect the direction of the meshes.
content_description: This web page provides a guide for generating aligned automatic retopology results in a 3D modeling environment, detailing the necessary steps and operations for effective remeshing.

title: Arrange Pattern with Arrangement Points/Flip Wrap Direction
content: ### ### ### ### Objective Arrangement Points are created based on the Bounding Volume surrounding the Avatar, and are arranged on the Avatar according to the Bounding Volume's curves. ※ Note: Precise arrangement is available by using Gizmo or Property Editor even after arranging with Arrangement Points. ### Location Avatar Display ▶ Show Arrangement Points ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: Avatar Display ▶ Show Arrangement Points → The Arrangement Points appear around the Avatar. 2. Select a Pattern and hover the mouse over an Arrangement Point. → A preview of the Pattern placement is being displayed (ver2.4.0). 3. Select a desired Arrangement Point. → The center of the Pattern is now being placed according to the selected Arrangement Point. → Symmetric Arrangement occurs as long as the Patterns and Arrangement Points have symmetry applied (ver3.0.0). ※ Note: #### Flip Wrap Direction Patterns that the length are longer than the Bounding Volume, such as cuffs, get arranged spiral. Right-click on patterns in the 3D window ▶ Click Flip Wrap Direction to flip its direction.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on arranging patterns around an Avatar using Arrangement Points based on the Avatar's Bounding Volume, with options for precise adjustments and symmetry features.

title: glTG 2.0 (glTF/GLB) File (ver 2026.0)
content: #### Ver 2026.0 **** Import or export glTF 2.0 (glTF/GLB) files. **** ## **Import** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ **glTF 2.0 (glTF/GLB)** 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. 3. Configure the settings and click **OK** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Open Type** | Open or add new files. **Object Type** | **Load as Avatar / Trim** | Load a glTF/GLB file as an avatar / trim. **Arrangement Points** **Auto Generate** | It automatically creates a Bounding Volume/Arrangement Points suitable for glTF/GLB. **Scale** | Type in the Scale or select the desired unit. * Commonly used default unit for glTF file is Meter. **Axis Conversion** | Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. **** ## **Export** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ **glTF 2.0 (glTF/GLB)** 2. Select the desired saving path and click **Save**. 3. Configure the settings and click **OK**. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Object** **** | **Select All Avatars/ Patterns/ Graphics/ Trims** | Select or deselect objects to be exported. **Single/ Multiple Objects** | Export the object as a single or multiple objects. **Thick/Thin** | Choose to export the object with the thickness or not. **Unified UV Coordinates** | A combined UV coordinates are also exported. **Option** | **Light** | Export along with lights **Garment Animation** | Export garment's animation. **Avatar Joint Animation** | Exports avatar joint keyframe animation. Bake Keyframes | Creates a keyframe for every frame. **Avatar Cache Animation** | Export cached avatar animation. **Basic** | **Scale** | Select the unit or the size of the object. ※ Note: Commonly used default unit for glTF file is Meter. **Axis Conversion** | Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. **Animation** | **Entire Region** | Exports the entire range where animation keys are set. **Play Region Only** | Exports only the animation within the specified playback range. **File** | **Save as glTF-Embedded** | Save textures as the glTF-Embedded format which includes texture files. **Save & Compress (ZIP)** ****| Diffuse Color Combined on Texture | When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting. ※ Note: Since the color is diffused to the UV map when the Combined UV Coordinates is selected, the menu is hidden. Exclude Ambient Map & Color (Modo) | Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting.. ※ Note: Since ambient maps and color are automatically excluded, the menu is hidden. **Save with Meta Data (extras)** | Save garments' patterns (mesh), physical properties, and sewing information as MetaData (XML).
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for importing and exporting glTF 2.0 (glTF/GLB) files, including detailed configuration options for optimal file management.

title: [Library] 18 Default MetaHuman Body Types Supported (ver 2024.0.173)
content: ### ![MetaHuman.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438430818969) ## **18 Default MetaHuman Body Types Supported (ver 2024.0.173)** Select a desired MetaHuman body type (*.avte) and create an outfit for your MetaHuman in Marvelous Designer before bringing the outfit to Unreal Engine as USD files. ### Steps You can find the MetaHuman body types and download it from the Library. ### Location Library ▶ Click Avatar Folder ▶ MetaHuman ▶ Double click to download a desired MetaHuman body types (*.avte) Note: These Metahuman body types are[ *.avte Encrypted Avatar file types ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358169252633)and cannot be exported out of the software. ## **End Result** * The MetaHuman body will appear in the 3D window based on the selected files you chose.

title: Line Tack on Avatar
content: ### Objective Create lines on Garment and avatar and tack to each other by lines. (Ver. MD7) ### Location 3D window tool bar Line tack on Avatar tool ### Operation 1. Select the tool according to the Location above. 2. Mouse over to a garment from 3D window. Point follows mouse cursor. 3. Double click on the garment where want to create start point of line / shape. Double click to complete the line / shape Double click on start point of line to create closed shape. Once a line is created on the garment, 3D garment will be transparent, can create line on the avatar directly. 4. Create second line/ shape. Once all the two lines / shapes have been created, connection line for line / shape will be displayed. 5. Click the simulation button. Two lines/ shapes tack to each other along the connection line. * During the creation of the line, pressing the Shift key will display the front, back, side center line and guide line of last point. * Press the Ctrl key to create curved line. * When creating a line, can cancel it from the last point by pressing the Delete key on Keyboard. Press the Esc / Ctrl+Z to cancel the whole point.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the 3D window toolbar to create and connect lines on garments and avatars in a virtual design environment.

title: Zoom In/Out, Rotation
content: ### Objective In Marvelous Designer, the mouse wheel and the right button can be used to zoom in, zoom out, and rotate the screen. The Maya and 3Ds Max view control methods are also supported alongside the default view control method and interface can be modified as needed and use differently. ### Operation #### Move Hold down the mouse wheel and drag to move the screen. If you are using Mac's Magic Mouse, please hold down the Alt key on the keyboard and click-and-drag the left mouse key. #### Zoom In/Out Scroll down (zoom in) and up (zoom out) the mouse wheel to zoom in and zoom out the screen. Or, hold down Alt Key on the keyboard and the left button of the mouse simultaneously and drag up (zoom out) or down (zoom in). ※ Note: Zoom in or zoom out using the + (zoom in) and - (zoom out) keys on the keyboard (ver2.4.0.) #### Rotate Hold down the right button of the mouse and drag to rotate the 3D window.
content_description: Discover how to effectively navigate and manipulate the 3D view in Marvelous Designer using various mouse controls, including zooming, moving, and rotating the screen.

title: Setup Guide for Marvelous Designer on Linux
content: ### Compatible operating system Marvelous Designer for Linux supports Rocky Linux 9.5 and its Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) equivalent. ### Setting up permission After downloading the installer, right-click the file and enable the 'Allow executing file as program' option. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/50923191155865) ### Installing NVIDIA Driver To download the correct NVIDIA driver for your Linux machine, please refer to [the official guideline by NVIDIA](https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/tesla/driver-installation-guide/index.html#red-hat-enterprise-linux). ### Launching Marvelous Designer Linux Double-click the AppImage file, or launch it from the terminal using the following command. Please note that you will need to replace the version number xxxx.y.zzz in the command accordingly. `./MarvelousDesigner_Enterprise_Online-x86_64_xxxx.y.zzz.AppImage` You can rename the AppImage file and launch Marvelous Designer using the modified name; however, we recommend using the default name with the specified version number.
content_description: This webpage provides essential instructions for installing and launching Marvelous Designer on Rocky Linux 9.5, including system compatibility, permission setup, and NVIDIA driver installation.

title: Move/Rotate Pattern with Gizmo
content: ### Objective Move or rotate Patterns, objects, Avatar Joints and etc. with the Gizmo. ### Location #### Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) #### Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'E' on keyboard ※ Note: Preferences for the Divided Gizmo can be accessed via: Main Menu ▶ User Setting ▶ 3D ▶ Gizmo ▶ Divided Gizmo ### Operation #### Move 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: #### Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) #### Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'E' on keyboard → The Gizmo appears. 2. Move by dragging in a desired direction. ※ Note: #### Move Y Axis Click > Drag the green arrow (pointing up) up and down to move the Pattern vertically. #### Move X Axis Click > Drag the red arrow (pointing right) left and right to move the Pattern horizontally. #### Move Z Axis Click > Drag the blue arrow (pointing forward) forward (upwards on the screen) or backwards (downwards on the screen) to pull or push the Pattern to the front and back. #### Yellow Square Box Free drifting to horizontal/vertical directions. ![Gizmo](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438002535449) #### Rotate 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: #### Unified Gizmo (Default Setup) 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) #### Divided Gizmo (User Setup) Select: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'Q' on keyboard Move: 3D Toolbar ▶Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'W' on keyboard Rotate: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Pattern (Simulation OFF) ▶ 'E' on keyboard → The Gizmo appears. 2. Mouse over the Gizmo's rotation axis. → The mouse cursor shape is now being replaced to (Rotate). 3. Click ▶ Drag in the desired direction to rotate the corresponding object. ※ Note: #### Rotate Y Axis Click > Drag the green radius left and right to rotate the Pattern centered on the vertical line. #### Rotate X Axis Click > Drag the red radius up and down to rotate the Pattern centered on the horizontal line. #### Rotate Z Axis Click > Drag the blue radius the Pattern with the central point as the axis. ![Gizmo](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438002843929)
content_description: Learn how to effectively move and rotate patterns, objects, and avatar joints using the Gizmo in your 3D design workspace.

title: [Fit Maps] Strain Map
content: **** The degree of deformation of the garment or fabric caused by external force is expressed as a percentage. **** 1. Long-press the ![Fit Maps Off Hover.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/56518820175513) **Fit Map** icon in the upper-left corner of the 3D Window and select the ![Fit Maps Strain Map Hover.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/56518836735385) **Strain Map**(Alt + 7) option. → The degree of deformation of the garment caused by external forces is displayed in color. 2. Refer to the following options in the Strain Map window to configure detailed settings. 3. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Global** | Absolute strain is displayed based on a fixed standard value, regardless of the fabric type. Global Mode is used to objectively check how much the pattern itself has physically deformed, independent of the fabric's specific properties. **Range** | The range between the base value (100%) and the user-defined fixed standard (Maximum) is divided into eight segments for visualization. You can customize the colors by selecting each individual color chip. **Fabric** | The strain is displayed based on the unique tensile limit of each fabric. This precisely reflects the material’s characteristics, allowing for a more accurate assessment of the fit. **Range** | The range between the base value (100%) and the unique tensile limit of each fabric is divided into eight segments for visualization. You can customize the colors by selecting each individual color chip. **Stretch** | By default, the limit for the actual wearable range is automatically calculated and applied based on the unique tensile properties of each fabric. The stretch limit is set based on the threshold where the fabric can no longer structurally expand when a consistently strong force is applied to all fabrics. In other words, this represents the point where it is judged "too uncomfortable to wear" in a real-life fit. For example, a stiff fabric reaches its limit even with minimal stretching, whereas a flexible fabric must stretch significantly more to reach its limit. **📝****Note:** If necessary, you can manually enter and configure the stretch limit. 4. Click a specific point on the simulated 3D garment to check the detailed values for that location. **Dominant Direction** This indicates the direction that has reached closest to the stretch limit. It serves as an indicator showing whether the greatest stress is being applied to the warp, weft, or bias of the fabric. **Actual Stretch** This is the absolute value showing how much the fabric has actually stretched in the indicated direction. **Force** This value is a percentage (%) representing how close the fabric is to its stretch limit, where 100% signifies the state at which the limit has been reached. A value of 100% means the fabric has reached its maximum allowable stretch, and any value exceeding 100% indicates that the limit has been surpassed.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions on using the Strain Map feature in Marvelous Designer to visualize and analyze the deformation of garments and fabrics under external forces, enabling precise fit assessments based on material characteristics.

title: What is the product version support policy for Marvelous Designer?
content: ### Q. What is the product version support policy for Marvelous Designer? A. Product support is available for the versions listed below. The latest product version receives regular updates with new features and hotfixes, along with fast technical support. The level of technical support may vary depending on the product version. Please refer to the table below for more details. **Product version** | **Build version** | **Support Range** ---|---|--- Marvelous Designer 2026 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 2026.0 | Technical Support Software Updates and patches Marvelous Designer 2025 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 2025.0 | Technical Support Software Updates and patches Marvelous Designer 2024 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 2024.0 | Technical Support Software Updates and patches Marvelous Designer 12 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 7.1 | Technical Support Software Updates and patches are NOT supported * There are two methods for requesting technical support: "[Contact Us](https://marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact)" and "[Community Forum](https://connect.clo-set.com/community/qna)." The support scope includes issues encountered during program installation and execution. * Please note that it may be difficult to provide support for issues arising from the difference between the supported version OS at the time of purchase and the current OS in use during installation or execution. *Please note that the [trade-in policy](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/support/news/view/f16869c1b54c4ed697f2721cddfe1340) from Enterprise Perpetual licenses to Annual type licenses are no longer available as of Jan 01 2026. **NOT supported product version** | **Build version** | **support** ---|---|--- Marvelous Designer 11 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 7.0 | Not supported Marvelous Designer 10 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 6.0 | Not supported Marvelous Designer 9 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 5.1 | Not supported Marvelous Designer 8 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 4.2 | Not supported Marvelous Designer 7 (Personal, Student, Enterprise, Academic) | above 3.2 | Not supported * Technical support and software updates and hotfixes have been discontinued, except for perpetual license holders, who will continue to receive limited assistance. * Limited assistance includes assistance with installer downloads and installations. * Versions below 7 cannot be downloaded via the website installer. If you have a perpetual license for a product version below 7, please[ contact our support team](https://marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact) for further assistance.

title: UI Changes (Above ver. 11)
content: ### ### ### **Layout Window** [Workspace Windows / Side Windows] Select Mode * Every window can be changed from one to another through the drop-down list at the top center of the window * Window switcher is not available after ver. 2025.0 → Windows can be accessed from Main Menu ▶ Window Duplicate Window * Select a Duplicate icon at the top right-hand corner of a window, and the window will be duplicated as a pop-up. [Workspace Windows] Set up the number of the Workspace Windows * You can set up the window view options at the bottom right-hand corner of the screen. * As many as four Workspace Window can be shown at one time. * With the shortcut 'Alt+W', you can switch between the current window layout and a full screen of the selected window . (ver. 12.1) [Side Windows] Close Windows * Only Side windows can be closed, not the Workspace windows. * Select X at the top right-hand corner to close the window. Show/Hide Window * Only Side windows can be either shown and hidden, not the Workspace windows. * Select the arrow on the top left-hand corner to hide the window. Its title will appear as a tab on either side of the screen after being hidden. * If you click on that tab, the window appears again. Arrange Windows * All pop-up windows can be arranged by dragging on either side of the window. Create Windows Tab * Each pop-up window can be dragged onto an existing side window to group them together. * Their title will appear as tabs at the bottom of the window. * You can select a tab to view each window in a group. ### **Toolbar** Arrange Toolbar * You can relocate the toolbar to the top, bottom, left, and right of a window by clicking the control handle on the leftmost side Show/Hide Toolbar * Toggle the Show/Hide Toolbar button at the far right of the view icons in each window to make it appear or disappear. Duplicate Tool Group * Move Mouse over a tool group to find sub-tools of the tool group. * A tool group can be duplicated as a pop-up by either clicking the dashed line with scissors in the tool group or by pressing the Enter key. Modular Editor * Modular Editor is added to the tool bar on the 2D window. * You can use the existing Modular Editor, by toggling the Modular Editor icon. ### **Main Menu** Duplicate the Menu list * A dash line will be shown if you click a main menu which can be duplicated as a pop-up. * If you either click the dashed line with scissors in a main menu or press the Enter key, the main menu will be duplicated as a pop-up. title: How can I delete the account?
content: Understand how to delete account on Marvelous Designer. 1. Delete account after unsubscribing current license/plan 2. Delete account immediately ## ## **Details** #### #### **1) Delete Account after unsubscribing current licenses** 1\. Visit “My Account” page from [**Marvelous Designer**](https://www.marvelousdesigner.com/mypage/account) to start the account deletion process. ![스크린샷 2025-05-21 오후 4.26.22.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438105606169) 2\. Click "Delete My Account" button at the bottom of "Account" tab. ![스크린샷 2025-05-21 오후 4.29.57.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438105832729) 3-1. Click "Delete" button to further proceed. ![스크린샷 2025-05-21 오후 4.33.44.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438091987993) _💡**Note:** If account is using Enterprise license on CLO / Marverlous Design or, account is seller_ _on CONNECT and there is an unsettled amount remaining, you won't be able to delete_ _the account directly. Please click**"Contact US"** button for further assistance._ _*For enterprise user, License ID can ONLY be deleted on the license admin page_ ![mceclip3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438078459545) 4\. Current license/plan will be displayed and must be canceled before account deletion. * All **CLO** and **MD** licenses, as well as any **CLO-SET paid plans** , must be unsubscribed in the area marked as **①**. * **You must leave any CLO-SET groups** in the area marked as **②**. _**💡 Note:** After canceling your licenses and plans, you will still be able to use the service until their expiration date. The “Next” button will become active **only after the end date.**_ ![mceclip6.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438078688665) #### **2) Delete Account immediately** 1. title: Marvelous Designer to MetaHuman: USD Garment Integration Workflow
content: This guide outlines the workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and integrating them with Unreal Engine **MetaHuman**. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0-Xj3E11GzM Step 1. Import USD Asset Step 2. Prepare MetaHuman Step 3. Create Cloth Asset Step 4. Configure Dataflow for Cloth Asset Step 5. Organize Assets Step 6. Create Outfit Asset Step 7. Configure Outfit Asset Step 8. Apply Outfit to MetaHuman ChaosCloth Asset Compatibility * * * ## Step 1. Import USD Asset ## ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799018460697) 1. In the **Content Drawer** , import your Clothing USD Asset created in Marvelous Designer into the desired folder. 2. Verify that the static meshes are correctly imported. ## Step 2. Prepare MetaHuman ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799018466585) 1. Locate your MetaHuman in the **Content Browser**. * Or, run it through the right-click Context Menu → MetaHuman → MetaHuman Character to create a new MetaHuman 2. **Double-click** the MetaHuman to open the **MetaHuman Editor**. 3. Export the MetaHuman as a **Combined Skeletal Mesh** : * MetaHuman Editor Main Menu → MetaHuman Creator → Export Combined Skel Mesh * Save this mesh inside the **Skeletal Meshes** folder of your USD asset directory. ## Step 3. Create Cloth Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799079787033) 1. In the **Static Meshes** folder: * **Right-click** → **Physics > Cloth Asset**. * Name it clearly (e.g., CA_name). 2. **Open Cloth Asset in Dataflow Editor** : * Right-click the Cloth Asset → **Open in Dataflow Editor (Experimental)**. 3. **Clean up nodes** : * Delete everything except: * USD Import * Transfer Skin Weights * Remesh * Remesh LOD2 (optional for extra LOD) * Cloth Asset Terminal. ## Step 4. Configure Dataflow for Cloth Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799641793433) 1. **Add Static Mesh Import Node** : * Right-click background → **Create Node: Static Mesh Import**. * Assign your USD static mesh to this node. 2. **Connect Nodes** : * Static Mesh Import → Transfer Skin Weights. * Transfer Skin Weights → Cloth Asset Terminal. * Also connect: * Transfer Skin Weights → Remesh → Collection LOD0. * Transfer Skin Weights → Remesh LOD2 → Cloth Asset Terminal (optional). 3. **Configure Transfer Skin Weights Node** : * Target Meshes: **Render Mesh**. * Render Mesh Transfer: **Skeletal Mesh**. * Transform Method: **Closest Point on Surface**. * Assign the **Combined Skeletal Mesh** to the Skeletal Mesh property. 4. **Preview** : * Switch the left window view to **Render** for visualization. ## Step 5. Organize Assets ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799881262873) 1. Create a new folder inside the Basic**Mesh** folder. 2. Move: * Static Mesh * Cloth Asset * Cloth Asset Node into this folder. ## Step 6. Create Outfit Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52799881264409) 1. In **Static Mesh Folder** : * **Right-click** → **Physics > Outfit Asset**. * Name it clearly (e.g., OA_name). 2. Select **Resizable Outfit Template** when prompted. 3. Move the Outfit Asset node into the folder created earlier. ## Step 7. Configure Outfit Asset ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52800581027609) 1. **Open Outfit Asset in Dataflow Editor** : * Double-click the Outfit Asset. 2. Change **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** from **Automatic** to **Manual**. 3. **Add Source Asset** : * Select **Sized Outfit Source** → Click **+**. * Drag the Cloth Asset into the Source Asset option. * Assign a size name. 4. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** and wait for completion. 5. Open **Source Body Slider** : * Drag and drop the Combined Skeletal Mesh. 6. Enable **Sized Outfit** checkbox to make it resizable. 7. Click **Evaluate Dataflow Graph** again, then switch back to **Automatic**. ## Step 8. Apply Outfit to MetaHuman ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/52800581029657) 1. Open MetaHuman Editor. 2. Go to the **Hair and Clothing** tab. 3. Drag and drop the **Outfit Asset** from the Content Drawer into the Outfit Clothing section. 4. In the Body tab, change the model's size parameters to adjust MetaHuman proportions, and confirm that the outfit adapts dynamically. 5. **Verify** that the outfit adjusts automatically to match the Metahuman's new size. ## ChaosCloth Asset Compatibility The use of ChaosCloth assets from USD data exported from Marvelous Designer is subject to the following compatibility restrictions based on the Unreal Engine version: * **Marvelous Designer 2025.0:** Compatible only with **UE 5.4**. * **Marvelous Designer 2025.2:** Compatible with **UE 5.6** and later version. * **UE 5.5:** Not compatible due to technical issues regarding simulation data. ※ Note: This issue is specific to **ChaosCloth**. Regular meshes and materials are unaffected.
content_description: This guide provides a step-by-step workflow for exporting garments from Marvelous Designer as USD and seamlessly integrating them with Unreal Engine's MetaHuman, ensuring compatibility and proper asset management.

title: 3D Pencil (Avatar)
content: **Ver 2026.0** **** Sketch directly on the avatar and turn your lines into patterns instantly. #### **Sketch** 1. Load an avatar in the 3D window to being sketching. 2. In the 3D toolbar, press and hold the **3D Pen (Avatar)** and switch to the **3D Pencil (Avatar)**. → The Sketch dialog appears, and the viewpoint switches to the front view. **※ Note:** To ensure proper conversion to 3D Pen after sketching, the 3D view is fixed to either the front or back view. Only zooming is available. 3. Click and drag on the avatar to sketch your design. 4. Change the type to **Eraser** , then click and drag over the area you want to remove. → The lines within the dragged area are removed. #### **Options** 1. Set the following options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Type** | **Pencil** | **Symmetry** | Applies symmetrical sketching based on the avatar’s center axis. **Conversion** **Guide** | Before converting to 3D Pen, you can see how your sketch will be converted. The segment points shown on the guide line are important, as areas without points will turn into curves. If you need a corner or a defined angle, make sure a point is present at that position. If a corner is missing a point, the edge may become rounded unintentionally. We recommend reviewing the guide and adjusting your lines to achieve the best results before converting. **Eraser** | **Size** | Adjust the eraser size to control how much is removed at once. **Viewpoint** | Switch the 3D viewpoint to either the front or back. #### **Convert to 3D Pen** 1. Click the **Convert to 3D Pen** in the Sketch dialog. → The lines drawn on the avatar are converted to 3D Pen, and the tool automatically switches to the **Edit 3D Pen (Avatar).** 2. Check the converted 3D Pen and edit[ ](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115008890367-Edit-3D-Pen-Avatar)it directly as needed. **※ Note:**__ For 3D Pens created by sketching on both the front and back simultaneously, flattening both sides automatically sews the front and back together.
content_description: "Discover the innovative 3D sketching tool that allows you to effortlessly create and convert designs on avatars into stunning patterns."

title: Pleats
content: ## **Objective** Create the desired shape of pleats to Patterns. ## **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Pleats.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51784511607961)Pleats** ## **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click to create a start point and an endpoint of a reference line of the pleats along Pattern Outlines. → A Pattern is divided into two. 3. Click on the side where the pleats will be added. → The Pleats window appears. 4. Configure the options and select OK. **Pleats Type** | Select the type of the pleats (Knife, Box, or Accordion). ---|--- **Specification** | Number of Pleats | Decide the number of pleats. Depth | Assign the depth of the pleats (the depth of folded pleats). Interval | Set the interval between pleats when there are two or more pleats. Reverse Direction | Reverse the direction where the pleats will be added. **Option** | Assign fold angles to the fold lines. Greater the difference between the angle of Outside Fold and Inside Fold, sharper the folds are. → The pleats are created on the Pattern. → If there is an Internal Line in the Pattern, it is also moved and rotated along with the Pattern. **※ Note:** * If the segment where pleats are to be created is sewn to another Pattern, the pleats will be automatically sewn in place based on the pleat type selected. If the segment is not sewn, use the **Pleats Sewing** tool to sew the pleats to the other Pattern. * Pleats are dependent on segment point locations. When a pleat is started between two segment points, it will not go further than the next segment point and will result in an error/ red color to indicate this.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and customizing pleats in 2D patterns using the designated tools in the software.

title: FABRIC PHYSICAL PROPERTIES: Adjust Bending-Weft/Warp
content: ### Objective Use Bending intensity which is the resistant against being bent, to adjust the stiffness of fabric. The higher the value, the stiffer it becomes such as denim and leather, and the lower the value, the more it becomes suitable for draping materials such as silk. The Bending intensity for the weft and warp directions can be set separately like the real fabrics. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Property Editor ▶ Physical Property ▶ Preset ▶ Bending-Weft/Warp Expressing materials with Weft (Horizontal) bending intensity ![B](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438785219737) Expressing materials with Warp (Vertical) bending intensity ![B](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438801346585)
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting fabric stiffness using bending intensity values for both weft and warp directions to achieve desired material characteristics in design applications.

title: Simulation Properties
content: ### Objective Configure the simulation properties for advanced scene settings. ### Location Object Browser ▶ ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358131961369) Scene ▶ Environment ▶ Simulation Properties Right-Click 3D background ▶ 3D Background Options ▶ Simulation Properties ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. → The simulation properties appear in the Property Editor. 2. Refer to the below table and edit the simulation properties as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- Use the Folder Icon to open the File Explorer to import a custom setting. Use the Save icon to save custom settings. Preset | Instead of selecting the [simulation mode](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232630937) from the 3D toolbar, you can choose predefined presets below are primarily used. * Normal (Default) * Animation (Stable) * Fitting (accurate Fabric) Time Step | This determines the time values calculated within the simulation engine. The smaller you set it, the more sophisticated it will be, but it will also require more calculations and will, resultingly, be slower. The default values are recommended. Simulations Per Frame (Simulation Quality) | When calculating cloth simulation for a given time step, this denotes how many substeps one simulation calculation is divided into. For example, if you are calculating a time step of 0.03 and number of simulation is 10, the actual time step will be 0.003. Simulating multiple times with these smaller time intervals ensures both more numerically accurate results and stable collision handling, but takes much longer. CG Finish Condition | Clothing simulation is the process of solving a large linear system. Large linear systems can be solved using a numerical analysis method called conjugate gradient method (CG). CG improves the accuracy of the answer through iterative calculations. The condition for CG ending can be set by the number of iterations or when the error (=residual) falls below a certain value. CG Iteration Count | Iteration: Because it repeats only a certain number of times and ends unconditionally, it is faster but may be less accurate. CG Residual | Residual: It is slower but can be more accurate because it stops when the error falls below a certain value. Self Collision Iteration Count | Defines the number of collision calculations for the clothing. More collision calculations produce more precise results, but they are also slower. Please use the default value. Air Damping | The resistance that the garment receives from the air. Gravity | Defines the most important gravity values in your simulation. If this value is adjusted, simulation results will become unrealistic. Please use the default value, unless you want to, for example, create a weightless simulation. Default is -9800 (0 results in no gravity and positive values can achieve other interesting results) Number of CPU in Use | This determines the number of physical cores within the CPU that will be used for the simulation. Marvelous Designer can technically use up to 12 cores, which are automatically defined based on your computer. Even if it is a high-end CPU with 16 cores, up to 12 can be used. This may vary depending on the CPU manufacturer and actual CPU products. This value is best also left at default. Nonlinear Simulation | Linear or non-linear is an important factor in all fields of computer graphics, simulation, rendering and engineering. By analogy, the real world is non-linear, but computer implementations are linear. Nonlinearity is a technique that makes things look very real, and simulating them this way is sophisticated, but slow. If Fitting simulation is run, this option is selected. t's slower because it's more complicated and requires a lot of calculations. **Collision Simulation Options** Ground | All of these are intended to simulate collisions and friction between the clothing and the avatar. Because Marvelous Designer calculates numerous contacts and collisions between the fabric and the body, the simulation looks natural and realistic. It is recommended that these values are also left at their default. ---|--- Avatar-Cloth Collision Detection | Toggle On/ Off * Triangle-vertex * Edge-Edge Self-Collision Detection | Toggle On/ Off * Triangle-vertex * Edge-Edge Avoidance Stiffness (adjustable property, default is [0.001000] ) Proximity Detection | Toggle On/ Off * Triangle-vertex * Edge-Edge **Collision Resolution Options** Intersection Resolution | Toggle on / off Allow Normal / Flipped Normal values to set direction and resolve intersecting mesh issues. ---|--- Layer Based Collision Detection | Toggle on / off Allow layers & Sublayers to set Collision values. (example: layer 1 will be on top of layers 0 and below) ※ Note: Use the Open &Save buttons on the top of the Property Editor to save, open, and reuse the settings.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for configuring and optimizing simulation properties within advanced scene settings in Marvelous Designer.

title: Troubleshooting "MSVCP100.dll was not found" Error Message.
content: ### Objective Learn how to resolve launch error with missing MSVCP100.dll This is caused by missing or outdated Visual C++ Redistributable which essential Windows component to running Marvelous Designer software. ![error](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438429828505) ### ### **How to solve** * Visit [Microsoft website](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-US/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist?view=msvc-170), then download and install the latest Visual C++ Redistributable. The X64 architecture is recommended. ### **Note** * In some cases, you may need to remove older versions of the Visual C++ Redistributables installed on your computer. * The Visual C++ Redistributable is backward compatible with older versions, so we recommend installing only the most recent version.
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide to resolve the launch error caused by the missing MSVCP100.dll file, ensuring successful operation of Marvelous Designer software through the installation of the latest Visual C++ Redistributable.
